A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain the main text and Appendices A–I. Text, equations, figures, tables, and examples can be matched reliably despite minor layout shifts.

before.justification: v1 reports original Qwen3-VL secret-disclosure experiments across four settings, including measured auditing rates in Tables 2–4 and additional quality analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original secret-disclosure experiments, numerical results in Tables 2–4, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The reasoning task-vector procedure and uniform, heuristic, and Fisher-based coefficient strategies remain unchanged in Section 3. No algorithm component, training objective, or inference procedure is revised.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four settings: MMLU answer metadata, Taboo secret words, Gender concealed beliefs, and SSC encoded behavioral constraints. Training and evaluation dataset coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the same coefficient strategies, layer-norm and global-norm random baselines, and prefill conditions. Bibliographic edits do not change which methods are evaluated.

E3.justification: Model sizes, training splits, amplification sweeps, 256-sample evaluations, generation settings, judges, and evaluation metrics are unchanged in Section 4 and the appendices.

E4.justification: Both retain the same amplification and coefficient analyses, prefill-composition tests, coherence validation, behavioral analyses, and example outputs. Appendix passages move without adding or removing analyses.

E5.justification: The 95% Wilson intervals, paired McNemar tests with Holm–Bonferroni correction, and Pearson correlation analyses are unchanged. Neither repeated-run nor seed reporting changes.

E6.justification: Reported numerical and qualitative results match throughout. For example, Table 2 retains 8B Taboo disclosure of 3.1% at alpha=1 and 8.6% at alpha=3; Table 3 retains 53.4% for SSC Prefill+OT (best) at alpha=3. Appendix results also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1, Equations 1–5, and the mathematical discussion in Appendix G are retained. No formal assumption, derivation, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about reasoning amplification, four experimental settings, model scaling, layer-wise attenuation, and composition with prefill attacks.

C2.justification: The proposed disclosure mechanisms, distinction between directionally protected and noise-fragile secrets, and interpretations of emergent behaviors remain unchanged. Section 6.3 retains the same limitations and proposed follow-up work.

D1.justification: Prompt templates, dataset identifiers, LoRA settings, optimization details, hardware, computation times, and judge prompts are unchanged. Their movement across pages adds no reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain the same. Revised entries for DF-Merge, LiNeS, and other references update bibliographic metadata; Section 2's descriptions and relationships to prior work are unchanged.

P1.justification: Several reference entries receive author, title, publication, or identifier edits, and Belrose's in-text citation changes from 2025 to 2023. The version/date stamp changes, while the main prose and section ordering remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Expanded reference entries cause limited reflow: B.3 begins on page 12 instead of 11, F.4 on page 14 instead of 12, and Appendix I on page 15 instead of 14. Figures and tables retain their designs, captions, and contents.

improvement.justification: v2 replaces Greenblatt's placeholder identifier '2412.xxxxx' with '2412.14093', adds an identifier for Arcuschin et al., and supplies fuller reference metadata. These changes improve source identification, while the reflow keeps several appendix passages together. The benefits are editorial; scientific evidence and limitations remain unchanged.
